newsitem.title: CANADA: Cambior sees stronger results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cambior sees stronger results in 1997.

text.p: Cambior Inc said on Wednesday that it expects stronger financial results in 1997, based on an increase in gold production to 550,000 ounces.

In 1996, Cambior produced 502,000 ounces of gold, a 13 percent increase from 1995. Cambior's profit forecast is also based on expectations of full sustainable levels of production for all of the company's major operations, it said.

Cambior plans capital expenditures of US$140 million for 1997 to support construction start-up on the Carlota project (US$80 million), for ongoing expenditures on producing assets (US$40 million), and for development projects (US$20 million).

"By mid-year, with the benefit of the completed feasibility studies on our major projects, we will be in a better position to establish their economic values and to define the optimum program development within Cambior's operating and financial capabilities," president and chief executive Louis Gignac said in a statement.
He said the company will continue to focus on the long- term development of gold operations by increasing its efforts and investments in exploration activities.

Cambior increased its exploration budget to US$18 million in 1997 from US$12 million in 1996. Exploration will target existing properties at Omai, including the Quartz Hill and Omai River concessions that were recently granted prospecting licences, the high gold potential of the Doyon and Mouska mines and the areas surrounding the Bouchard-Hebert mine.
Prospective gold exploration activities will concentrate on high potential properties in Mexico, the Guiana Shield and the Peruvian Cordillera, Cambior said.
The first half of 1997 will be very active with the completion of feasibility studies on major projects at El Pachon, La Granja, Gross Rosebel and Metates, the company said.

At the Gross Rosebel project, the company expects drilling results to confirm an increase in gold mining reserves to its target of 2 million ounces for the project. At El Pachon, the feasability study will be completed on the basis of the recently announced reserves of 882 million tonnes grading 0.62 percent copper.
At La Granja, an important increase in proven and probable mining reserves is expected with the completion of a reserve update in the first quarter, Cambior said.

At year end 1996, Cambior's gold hedging program had a net position ensuring a minimum price of US$462 an ounce on 410,000 ounces of gold over the next five years, it said. Over 1996, Cambior realized an average price of US$423 an ounce of gold, for a premium of US$35 over the average 1996 market price of US$388 an ounce, the company said.
